adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 / lib/email/message_builder.rb — unsubscribe_link now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} unconditionally, but other callers with add_unsubscribe_link: true (digest emails, mailers not going through send_notification_email) never pass unsubscribe_url, so I18n.t raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and those emails fail to build; the spec fixture change papers over this regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml) to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` only has `site_name`, `base_url`, and `user_preferences_url` by default (lib/email/message_builder.rb) and does not define `unsubscribe_url` unless a caller passes it. The spec had to be updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, indicating calls with only `add_unsubscribe_link: true` would now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to build the email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 + config/routes.rb:441 — state-changing unsubscribe action is exposed as a plain GET with check_xhr skipped, so it has no CSRF protection; a third-party page embedding an to the URL or a browser link prefetcher can silently mute or downgrade a logged-in user's topic subscription

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topics#unsubscribe` action that mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`s it, but it is routed only via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`. Because this is a state-changing operation over GET, it would not be protected by Rails’ CSRF mechanisms (which generally apply to non-GET), making it triggerable by cross-site requests (e.g., embedded image/link prefetch).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:106-112 — the mutation runs on every request with a two-step ladder (watching/tracking → regular → muted), so refreshing the confirmation page or a browser re-issuing the request silently mutes the topic; no idempotence and no confirmation step

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the GET request mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` every time it is hit: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it is set to `:regular`, otherwise it is set to `:muted` (lines shown in the diff under `def unsubscribe`). This creates a non-idempotent “ladder” for users starting at tracking/watching: first visit changes to regular, and a refresh/second request then changes regular → muted. Since the route is a GET (`get ... => "topics#unsubscribe"`) and there is no confirmation/state check, reloading or automatic retries can silently further change the user’s notification state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:26 — ensure_logged_in on a non-XHR GET gives a logged-out user clicking the email link Discourse's 403 'not logged in' page instead of a login redirect, dead-ending the primary email-client use case

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `unsubscribe_url` into notification emails (mailer passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, server locale text includes a per-topic unsubscribe link), but the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action is added to `requires_login` and relies on `current_user` (e.g., `current_user.id`). That means a logged-out user clicking the email link cannot complete the unsubscribe flow at all (they’ll be blocked by auth), making the new email link effectively nonfunctional unless already authenticated. The specific claim about a 403 vs redirect can’t be proven from this diff alone, but the core issue (email link requires login) is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:114 — writing tu.notification_level and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so no notification_level_change is published on MessageBus and notifications_reason_id is not updated to user_changed; open topic tabs show a stale level and the route nulls details.notificationReasonText client-side to work around stale reason text

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `tu.notification_level = ...` followed by `tu.save!`, rather than using `TopicUser.change(...)` (which in this diff clearly publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` when `notification_level` is set). So the specific point that this path will not publish the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is verifiable from the diff. However, claims about `notifications_reason_id` being updated to `user_changed` and the client-side `details.notificationReasonText` nulling being a workaround for a stale reason are not directly evidenced by this diff, making the overall impact less strictly verifiable as a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — email copy says clicking will 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic', but for watching/tracking users the action only drops them to Regular where replies, mentions and quotes still notify; copy overpromises relative to behavior

adjudication.rationale: The new email copy in config/locales/server.en.yml says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", but the implemented action in TopicsController#unsubscribe only toggles TopicUser.notification_level between :regular and :muted (it downgrades > :regular to :regular, else to :muted). For users currently tracking/watching, this does not fully stop all notifications related to the topic (it just returns them to regular), so the message overpromises relative to the behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — server preloads topic_<id> into the store, but the Ember route ignores it and calls PostStream.loadTopicView, causing a second full topic-view fetch on every unsubscribe page load

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action ends by calling `perform_show_response`, and `perform_show_response` (HTML branch) does `store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", ...)` and renders `:show`. However, the new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` always does `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` in `model()`, rather than consuming any preloaded `topic_<id>` payload. From the diff, that implies an avoidable extra topic-view JSON fetch on unsubscribe page load (a performance/architecture issue, not necessarily broken behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/ — no controller spec covers TopicsController#unsubscribe (level transitions, missing TopicUser row, slug redirect, logged-out behavior), and no MessageBuilder spec covers add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url, which is the case that currently breaks

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (new route/action with redirect logic and notification_level toggling) but the only test change shown is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb`; there is no new controller spec added in this diff to exercise unsubscribe edge cases. Also, `config/locales/server.en.yml` changes `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, while `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` still calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` with no default for `unsubscribe_url`; the updated spec now always supplies `unsubscribe_url`, but there is no coverage for the (potentially breaking) case `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`.
